newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Oil appoints new chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Oil appoints new chief executive.

text.p: Oil production and exploration firm Enterprise Oil Plc on Tuesday announced it had appointed a senior British Gas manager to become its new chief executive.
Pierre Jungels, who has held his job as British Gas's managing director of production and exploration for less than a year, will take up his new post on January 1.
Enterprise has been looking for a couple of years to find a chief executive to replace Graham Hearne, who will continue as chairman after having combined both positions since 1991.
To relieve Hearne, Enterprise in 1994 appointed Mike Pink as chief operating officer. Pink, 59, will retire at the start of the new year.
As it is company policy to have no executives older than 60, Pink was not considered to become chief executive, Enterprise said.
"Mike Pink has made an outstanding contribution to the operational success of Enterprise over the past two and a half years," Hearne said in a statement.
"Today's announcement is significant in that Pierre (Jungels) will have the responsibility of leading the group as chief executive into the next stage of growth," he added.

Enterprise, which failed to acquire rival LASMO in a bitter struggle in 1994, is currently expanding its operations from its North Sea base into Norway, Italy, the Gulf of Mexico, South America and the Middle East.
